newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian banker's wife New Socialist Idea dies.
newsitem.headline: Italian banker's wife New Socialist Idea dies.

text.p: Idea Nuova Socialista (New Socialist Idea), the wife of Italy's most powerful and most secretive banker, has died, the leftist newspaper L'Unita reported on Friday.
Known as Idea for short, she was married to Enrico Cuccia, honorary chairman of top merchant bank Mediobanca, which has a stake in virtually every major industry.
The obsessively secretive group declined comment but L'Unita said the office where deaths are registered confirmed that Idea Cuccia died in Milan on October 12. Her age was not known.

New Socialist Idea was a daughter of Alberto Beneduce who, as chairman of state holding company IRI, was one of Italy's most influential industrialists. He was considered by some a key adviser to wartime fascist dictator Benito Mussolini.
Like Mussolini, Beneduce had socialist origins which he highlighted in the choice of names for his daughters. Idea's sisters were called Proletarian Victory and Free Italy.

Idea met Cuccia in her father's salon, married him in June 1939 and had two daughters and a son, all with more mainstream Italian names. She shunned glamorous premieres or glitzy outings and the family led a modest and intensely private life.
